label: Cisco 8865
description: Cisco IP Phone 8865, the 720p-video flagship of the 8800 series, with a 5-inch 800x480 display, five programmable line keys and Intelligent Proximity pairing to a mobile. It carries an internal two-port 10/100/1000 switch for the phone and a co-located PC, draws 802.3at class-4 power on the LAN port, and adds an integrated 802.11a/b/g/n/ac Wi-Fi client so it can also sit on the WLAN with no cable at all.
notes: Datasheet: 'An internal 2-port Cisco Ethernet switch allows for a direct connection to a 10/100/1000BASE-T Ethernet network ... through an RJ-45 interface with single LAN connectivity for both the phone and a co-located PC', 'IEEE Power over Ethernet class 4 is supported. The phone is compatible with IEEE 802.3af, 802.3at and UPOE switch blades and supports both CDP and LLDP-PoE'. Class 4 is the 25.5 W 802.3at reservation - the phone will boot on an af port but with reduced features, which is exactly the misconfiguration a lab wants to reproduce. Wi-Fi table: 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 2.4/5 GHz, 802.11r FT and CCKM, WPA2-Enterprise; 867M models a 2x2 80 MHz ac link. Separate 802.1Q VLANs per PC and voice port; two USB ports, AUX and 3.5 mm jack not modelled.
